stories.title: W. Valley Data Center Developer Building Massive Energy System
stories.excerpt: For data centers to make their way through the permitting process, the developer most likely will have to provide power for the project without taxing current delivery systems. Copia Power is promoting a plan to do just that in Tonopah, a town about an hour west of Phoenix. The Phoenix Business Journal reports Copia Power, which develops, builds and operates grid-connected power and data center infrastructure, is working to rezone about 3,100 acres near Tonopah in the far West Valley for its latest project, the Belmont Energy Center. Most of the project site – about 2,860 acres – would be for utility-scale solar energy generation, while about 320 acres would be used for a gas generation facility, BESS and data centers. The project is backed by a $1.7 billion construction loan and has a power purchase agreement with APS. It’s expected to be operational within the next year. The post W. Valley Data Center Developer Building Massive Energy System appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Copia Power rezoning 3,100 acres near Tonopah, Arizona (60 miles west Phoenix) for Belmont Energy Center
$1.7B construction loan backing utility-scale solar, gas, BESS, and data center infrastructure; operational within 12 months
APS power purchase agreement eliminates grid strain; data centers attract tech talent and corporate demand to West Valley
stories.summary: Copia Power is developing a $1.7 billion integrated energy and data center project on 3,100 acres near Tonopah in Phoenix's far West Valley, with 2,860 acres for solar, 320 acres for gas/BESS/data centers, backed by APS offtake and expected online within a year. The project solves permitting constraints by providing dedicated power infrastructure.
stories.impact: Major data center and power infrastructure draw will accelerate population and job migration to West Valley submarkets (Tonopah, Goodyear, Buckeye); multifamily developers should acquire land and begin underwriting renter-demographic projects in 10–20 mile radius now, ahead of corporate campus and tech worker influx over next 24–36 months. West Valley rents will compress near-term but rebound sharply once data center operations ramp and supply lags demand.

stories.title: Affinius Capital Lends $177M for Multifamily Asset Buy in New Jersey, Yonkers
stories.excerpt: A joint venture between Lincoln Property Company, Saber-Hightower and Waterfall Asset Management has sealed $177.25 million of acquisition financing for the purchase of two multifamily properties in the New York metropolitan area, Commercial Observer has learned. Affinus Capital provided the debt package for the sponsorship’s purchase of the 262-unit Edgewater Harbor property in Edgewater, N.J., and the soon-to-be completed 147-unit Trilogy Lofts at Tuckahoe project in Yonkers, N.Y. The deal involved a $124 million loan for Edgewater Harbor and $53.4 million of acquisition debt for Trilogy Lofts. The joint venture of Lincoln Property Company, Saber-Hightower and Waterfall Asset Management acquired both properties from National Resources as part of a $450 million acquisition of four tri-state region properties encompassing more than 4 million square feet, CO previously first reported. “Edgewater and Trilogy Lofts represent a compelling opportunity to invest in high-quality, well-located multifamily assets in supply-constrained, transit-oriented submarkets with durable renter demand,” David Greenburg, managing director at Affinius Capital, said in a statement. “Waterfall Asset Management, Lincoln Property Company and Saber-Hightower bring institutional scale, local market expertise, and a proven track record of value-add execution that positions this portfolio for long-term performance.” Cushman & Wakefield negotiated the financing with a team consisting of John Alascio, Alex Hernandez, Brad Domenico, Chuck Kohaut and Mitch Rothstein. C&W also represented the seller in the acquisition with a Northeast capital markets team of Andy Merin, Frank DiTommaso and Ryan Dowd. Located at 45 River Road 6 miles from Midtown Manhattan, Edgewater Harbor features 60,500 square feet of retail space anchored by a Sprouts Farmers Market slated to open in 2027. Community amenities include fitness centers, rooftop decks, coworking space and an outdoor pool. Trilogy Lofts at 1 Sca
bullets: Lincoln/Saber-Hightower/Waterfall JV closed $177.25M debt for two NY metro multifamily properties via Affinius Capital
Edgewater Harbor (262 units, Edgewater, NJ): $124M; Trilogy Lofts (147 units, Yonkers, NY, near-completion): $53.4M
Part of larger $450M, 4-property tri-state acquisition; transit-oriented, supply-constrained submarkets confirm investor confidence in NY metro multifamily
stories.summary: A joint venture between Lincoln Property Company, Saber-Hightower, and Waterfall Asset Management secured $177.25 million in acquisition financing from Affinius Capital for two multifamily properties in the New York metro area: Edgewater Harbor (262 units in Edgewater, NJ) and the newly completed Trilogy Lofts (147 units in Yonkers, NY). The deal is part of a $450 million acquisition of four tri-state properties totaling over 4 million square feet.
stories.impact: Capital availability and investor appetite for well-located, transit-oriented NY metro multifamily remains strong despite broader credit stress; bridge financing at scale signals expected rents and NOI growth in Yonkers and Edgewater submarkets. Developers with shovel-ready, transit-proximate sites in supply-constrained NY submarkets should accelerate capital raises and pre-leasing, as institutional buyers are actively acquiring Class A assets.

stories.title: Office CMBS Delinquencies Surpass September 2012’s All-Time High
stories.excerpt: The office CMBS delinquency rate rose to a new all-time high of 8.89% in July 2026, surpassing the previous peak of 8.83% recorded in September 2012 and up from 8.0% a year earlier, reported Fitch Ratings. Fitch’s overall U.S. CMBS delinquency rate increased 16 basis points to 3.49% in July from 3.33% in June, due primarily to new office delinquencies and the default of a large mixed-use portfolio SASB loan New 60+ day delinquency volume increased to $2.82 billion in July from $2.09 billion in June, led by office (40%, $1.12 billion), mixed-use (26%, $728 million), multifamily (14%, $405 million) and retail (10%, $274 million). Term defaults accounted for 67% ($1.88 billion) of new delinquencies, while maturity defaults represented 33%. Resolution volume declined to $1.54 billion in July from $1.63 billion in June. July resolutions included $785 million of loan liquidations, $677 million of loans brought current and $77 million of previously 60+ days delinquent loans removed from Fitch’s index after improving to 30 days delinquent. The post Office CMBS Delinquencies Surpass September 2012’s All-Time High appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Office CMBS delinquency hit all-time high 8.89% in July 2026, surpassing Sept 2012 peak of 8.83%; up from 8.0% YoY
New 60+ delinquencies $2.82B in July vs. $2.09B in June; multifamily delinquencies $405M (14% of volume), up from prior month
Overall CMBS delinquency rate 3.49% in July; office crisis spreading to adjacent asset classes and debt markets
stories.summary: The office CMBS delinquency rate surged to an all-time high of 8.89% in July 2026, exceeding the September 2012 financial crisis peak of 8.83% and rising 89 basis points year-over-year. New 60+ day delinquencies totaled $2.82 billion in July, with office accounting for 40% ($1.12 billion), followed by mixed-use (26%), multifamily (14%, $405 million), and retail (10%). Overall U.S. CMBS delinquency rose to 3.49% in July from 3.33% in June.
stories.impact: Multifamily delinquency volume ($405M, 14% share) is growing; contagion risk from office/mixed-use distress into multifamily debt markets is real, especially for cross-collateralized portfolios and mixed-use developments. Spreads and pricing for multifamily CMBS/bridge financing will tighten further; developers seeking capital should expect higher coupons, tighter underwriting, and increased equity requirements through 2026–2027. Acquisition opportunities in distressed mixed-use and adaptive-use office-to-multifamily conversions will emerge as lenders liquidate and sponsor capital dries up.

stories.title: Return to Lender: Week of August 20, 2026
stories.excerpt: Willow Grove Park Mall is set to be sold to a partnership of three New York firms, the Philadelphia Business Journal reported. Namdar Realty Group, Mason Asset Management and CH Capital Group are under contract to acquire the Montgomery County retail property. A representative for mall owner PREIT told the Business Journal that “a lender-directed sale process is underway and expected to be completed in the near term.” PREIT’s lender, PGIM Inc., listed the property’s debt for sale earlier this year after the Philadelphia company’s $170-million loan on Willow Grove Park Mall matured. Kingswood Center ($65.5 million | COMM 2018-COR3 | CMBX.12) liquidated this month via a discounted payoff, according to Morningstar Credit The resolution resulted in a $46.6-million loss on the loan. When factoring in non-recoverable advances, $53.7 million of losses hit the bonds, wiping out classes H-RR and G-RR and writing down F-RR by about 25%. The loan was backed by a 129,000-square-foot mixed-use building in Brooklyn. It was in special servicing since May 2023 after occupancy fell to 35%. Baltimore-based Atapco Properties has purchased Charlestowne North Apartments in Greenbelt, MD, a 178-unit affordable housing complex that has long faced serious financial and maintenance issues tied to its previous owner’s loan distress. The company bought the nine-story building for $22.6 million from Freddie Mac late last month, reported the Baltimore Business Journal. The price works out to roughly $126,000 a unit. The Pittsburgh Business Times reported that three office buildings totaling351,000 square feet at Parkway Center are scheduled to be auctioned off starting on August 24, according to a listing on TenX. The buildings are being sold at auction as part of a larger strategy by an investment sales team at JLL based in Pittsburgh and led by Mark Popovich. stories.title: H-E-B Scores Sizable Tax Break for SA Warehouse Expansion
stories.excerpt: H-E-B is planning a $635 million expansion to its Super Regional Center near Foster Road and East Houston Street in Bexar County. As part of the deal, Bexar County has voted to approve a deal that will reduce the company’s county property-tax bill by more than $15 million over the life of the ten-year agreement. The San Antonio Business Journal reports that county leaders who support the incentive said the agreement is meant to encourage long-term industrial investment and job growth on the East Side. H-E-B built a 1.6-million-square-foot regional warehouse at the site in 2018 and added another plant in 2024. H-E-B has suggested that the latest additions will include a bakery plant, a refrigerated warehouse and a returned-goods center at the campus. The company has said the facility already employs about 1,400 workers. The expansion could add 720 new jobs. The post H-E-B Scores Sizable Tax Break for SA Warehouse Expansion appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: H-E-B $635M warehouse/logistics expansion at Foster Road/E. Houston, Bexar County (San Antonio area)
10-year tax break worth $15M+; bakery plant, refrigerated warehouse, returns center; 720 new jobs expected
Existing 1.6M SF facility (2018) + 2024 plant addition signals supply-chain consolidation and workforce concentration in East Side industrial corridor
stories.summary: H-E-B is investing $635 million in an expansion of its regional hub near Foster Road and East Houston Street in Bexar County (San Antonio), including bakery, refrigerated warehouse, and returns processing facilities. Bexar County approved a 10-year tax incentive reducing H-E-B's property tax bill by over $15 million, supporting the company's plan to add 720 jobs to an existing workforce of 1,400 at the campus.
stories.impact: Major supply-chain employer consolidation and job growth on San Antonio's East Side; 720 new warehouse/logistics jobs will drive renter demand in East San Antonio and surrounding suburbs (New Braunfels, Cibolo, Seguin corridors). Developers should acquire multifamily land within 5–10 miles of the Foster/E. Houston cluster and underwrite workforce housing (market-rate and affordable) with expected absorption lag of 18–24 months post-hiring. Tax incentive signals municipal commitment to industrial growth, creating secondary opportunity for TIF/PILOT-enabled mixed-use development near logistics nodes.

stories.title: PGIM Loans $83M to Refi 325-Unit New Jersey Apartment Complex
stories.excerpt: The final piece to a 1,300-unit apartment portfolio refinancing has been sealed. Commercial Observer can first report that Capodagli Property Company has secured $82.6 million to refinance Meridia Roselle Park 10, a 325-unit Class A multifamily complex in Roselle, N.J. PGIM provided the debt, structured as a bridge loan, while Greystone Capital Advisors’ Drew Fletcher, Bryan Grover, Miryam Reinitz-Kops and Jesse Kopecky arranged the transaction. The deal follows $287 million in cross-collateralized bridge financing PGIM had provided for four other Class A, multifamily assets in New Jersey throughout 2025. In total, PGIM provided $369.5 million in debt for a 1,340-unit multifamily portfolio comprised of Meridia Village Commons at 209 Valley Street in South Orange, N.J.; Meridia Pompton Lakes at 61 Wanaque Avenue in Pompton Lakes, N.J.; Meridia Linden 1001 at 1001 West Elizabeth Avenue in Linden, N.J.; and Meridia Little Ferry at 110 Bergen Turnpike in Little Ferry, N.J. Meridia Roselle Park 10 is at 10 West Westfield Avenue in Roselle Park, N.J., a suburb not far from Newark Liberty International Airport and 25 miles southwest of Times Square in Manhattan. Greystone’s Fletcher said in a statement that by breaking the cross-collateralized structure into separate deals, Capodagli Property Company was able to refinance each asset “on consistent terms as each came online,” giving each deal flexibility to seek out permanent financing at its own rate. “Completing this facility reflects the strength of our long-term relationship with Capodagli and PGIM’s continued conviction in their platform,” said Fletcher. Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commercialobsever.com.
bullets: PGIM provided $82.6M bridge loan to refinance Meridia Roselle Park 10 (325 units, Roselle Park, NJ Class A)
Final closing of $369.5M cross-collateralized portfolio financing covering five Meridia Class A properties (1,340 units) across NJ through 2025
Bridge structure and scale ($287M in prior tranches) confirms institutional lenders remain active in NJ multifamily, despite credit stress elsewhere
stories.summary: Capodagli Property Company closed a $82.6 million bridge loan from PGIM to refinance Meridia Roselle Park 10, a 325-unit Class A complex in Roselle Park, NJ. This completed a $369.5 million cross-collateralized portfolio financing spanning five Class A Meridia properties (1,340 units total) across New Jersey, with prior tranches of $287 million provided by PGIM throughout 2025.
stories.impact: Bridge financing availability for stabilized, Class A NJ multifamily assets remains robust, signaling strong sponsor conviction on rents and exit timing in the next 24–36 months. Developers with near-stabilization assets in high-barrier-to-entry NJ submarkets (South Orange, Pompton Lakes, Linden, Little Ferry, Roselle Park) have a refinancing/recapitalization window before rate volatility and cap-rate expansion narrow lender appetite. Rate locks and term certainty should be pursued immediately; anticipate 150–200 bps spread compression if Fed cuts materialize, creating 2027 refi opportunity for Class A product.

stories.title: Mamdani Wants to Add 18K New Homes on Staten Island
stories.excerpt: There’s a joke about how Staten Island got its name. Dutch settlers sailing into New York Harbor saw the 14-mile land mass and exclaimed “Is zat an island?” (You have to read it with the accent.) Is it the reality of how one of New York City boroughs got its name? No, but as the saying goes, “When the legend becomes fact, print the legend.” Fast forward to 2026, and New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has some big plans for the little island across the harbor from Manhattan. He is hoping to see a 9.5 percent growth in new homes on Staten Island over the next five years, or about 17,675 new homes across the borough, according to a growth plan from the Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) released Wednesday. “As the city commits to ambitious housing action through the Block by Block plan, the draft Fair Housing Growth Strategy provides a framework for measuring need and understanding where we should grow, with fair housing at its center,” Sideya Sherman, director of the Department of City Planning, said in a statement. Staten Island is broken up in three segments: North Shore, Mid-Island and South Shore. The South Shore and Mid-Island are the island’s least dense areas. However, residents and elected officials on the South Shore have historically pushed back on more residential development in their neighborhoods, so the mayor could be facing an uphill battle. “Staten Island is probably the most perfect place in the world because you’re 20 or 40 minutes away from the largest city in the country, but at the same time it’s like being in New England,” Stuart Saft, a real estate lawyer with Holland & Knight, previously told Commercial Observer. “I’ve been to Staten Island, and it’s a magnificent place to be.” The mayor isn’t just targeting housing growth on Staten Island over the next five years, mind you. bullets: NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani targets 17,675 new homes on Staten Island (9.5% growth) over next 5 years via HPD Fair Housing Growth Strategy
Block by Block housing initiative and citywide Fair Housing Growth Strategy framework prioritize supply in underutilized boroughs

stories.summary: NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani released a Fair Housing Growth Strategy aiming to add approximately 17,675 new homes (9.5% growth) to Staten Island over the next five years as part of the city's broader Block by Block housing plan. The strategy positions Staten Island as a priority growth market under HPD's framework for measuring housing need and identifying optimal neighborhoods for development.
stories.impact: This is a clear citywide signal to accelerate multifamily development on Staten Island, which has historically underutilized zoning and lower density than other boroughs; expect rezoning, CEQR streamlining, and discretionary variance approvals to accelerate in 2026–2027. Developers with land banks or control positions in Staten Island neighborhoods (especially near transit: St. George, Tompkinsville, Stapleton) should fast-track entitlement and begin marketing to institutional capital and HNW sponsors. 17,675-unit target implies ~3,500 units/year; supply will lag demand, supporting rent growth and value-add acquisition opportunity through 2028–2030.

stories.title: Planet Fitness Takes 15K SF at Coney Island Residential Development
stories.excerpt: Wake up, it’s time for a workout. Planet Fitness has inked a 14,500-square-foot retail lease at the base of a new residential tower in Coney Island, Brooklyn, with Cammeby’s International Group and Rybak Development. Planet Fitness will move into the space at 532 Neptune Avenue next year on a 10-year lease with an asking rent of $65 per square foot, according to the New York Business Journal, which first reported the deal. Planet Fitness was represented by CBRE, while ownership was represented by Commercial Acquisitions. The names of the brokers on both sides of the deal were not immediately available. The brokerages did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s requests for comment. Planet Fitness has nearly 50 gyms in New York City across all five boroughs. The company did not immediately respond to CO’s request for comment. Cammeby’s and Rybak completed the three-tower, 499-unit residential complex at 532 Neptune late last year, featuring studio to three-bedroom homes. Some 30 percent of those units are designated as affordable housing. The development has 758,600 square feet of residential space, 40,368 square feet of ground-floor commercial space and 20,722 square feet of community facilities. The two developers aren’t stopping their work in Coney Island anytime soon, either, as Cammeby’s and Rybak submitted a rezoning application in March to build two 22-story residential buildings with a total of 703 units at 3030 Ocean Parkway and 400 Neptune Avenue. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Planet Fitness leased 14,500 SF at 532 Neptune Avenue, Coney Island (Brooklyn) on 10-year term at $65/SF
Cammeby's/Rybak completed 499-unit, three-tower residential complex (studios to 3BR) in Q4 2025; 30% unit affordability
Anchor retail tenant signals strong foot-traffic demand and developer confidence in mixed-use residential-retail absorption in Coney Island
stories.summary: Planet Fitness signed a 14,500-square-foot lease at 532 Neptune Avenue in Coney Island, Brooklyn, in the base of a newly completed three-tower residential development by Cammeby's International Group and Rybak Development. The 10-year lease is at $65 per square foot, and Planet Fitness will open in 2027. The residential complex, completed in late 2025, contains 499 units (studios to three bedrooms) with 30% affordable units.
stories.impact: Strong anchor retail tenant (Planet Fitness) at $65/SF confirms robust foot-traffic and renter demand in Coney Island mixed-use product; availability of affordable units (30%) did not deter national brand from premium base rent, signaling mixed-income submarkets support higher retail rents. Developers evaluating mixed-use development in underutilized Brooklyn neighborhoods (Sunset Park, Astoria, Flatbush corridors) should prioritize retail anchors with broad appeal; retail spread compression in mixed-use reflects underpriced residential rental growth relative to retail opportunity. Coney Island's precedent validates 30% affordable + 70% market-rate rent mix as pro-forma friendly for institutional capital.

stories.title: Get to Know the Broker: Jonathan Stein of Douglas Elliman
stories.excerpt: For Jonathan Stein, the best is yet to come. Stein, 43, joined the real estate game in 2015 after spending time in the private equity space and then going on the road with his best friend’s rock band, Phantogram, as the tour manager. Now, he runs the Jonathan Stein Team at Douglas Elliman. Stein oversees a group of eight brokers at the firm, which has worked on deals ranging from $1 million to over $45 million. When former New York Mets and current Philadelphia Phillies pitcher Zack Wheeler needed to sell his SoHo penthouse at 73 Wooster Street, Stein and team member Gavin Shiminski stepped in, helping the major leaguer sell the unit for $26 million. It was one of the five largest sales in New York City in July. The road to such a successful real estate career wasn’t easy, but Stein said real estate is an amalgamation of his favorite things: design, architecture, mixing different personalities, and working well with people. “I got into real estate the old fashioned way — my life blew up and I needed a new career,” he said. “I was waiting tables at a buddy’s restaurant looking for what was going to come next. A friend suggested real estate and I loved the idea.” Commercial Observer caught up with Stein in August for “Get to Know the Broker,” a series where we connect with residential brokers to learn more about what makes them tick. This conversation has been edited for length and clarity. Commercial Observer: What has been the biggest deal of your career? Jonathan Stein: I haven’t done it yet. Check back next year. What is your career Everest? Doing my own development project. What’s something you think people would be surprised to learn about you? I grew up on a farm in a town of 170 people. We raised cattle and pigs, and I showed pigs in 4-H as a kid to help earn money for college. What’s your go-to takeout order? Sushi from my neighborhood omakase spot. What TV show are you currently binging? “All Creatures Great and Small.” What is your silliest pet peeve? When
